instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionStyles.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major (line 196): Paste styles cannot reset a sized arrow to the default size, so FR-11 fails for that case. If the source arrow has the default size and the target has, for example, "large", the update is `{ startArrowhead, endArrowhead, arrowheadSize: undefined }`. newElementWith skips undefined values when it checks for changes and returns the element unchanged when nothing changed (mutateElement.ts:156-172). So when the start and end arrowheads already match, the target keeps "large". If the arrowheads differ, the key is only set to undefined. actionChangeArrowheadSize works around this same newElementWith behaviour, but paste styles does not. The existing test only covers pasting a small size onto a default arrow. Confidence: high (read from newElementWith's source). — fix: When `arrowheadSize === undefined` and the target has a non-default size, drop the key and force a version bump, as actionChangeArrowheadSize does: `const { arrowheadSize: _, ...rest } = newElement; newElement = newElementWith(rest as typeof newElement, { startArrowhead, endArrowhead }, true)`. Otherwise keep the current call. Add a test in packages/excalidraw/tests/arrowheadSize.test.tsx that copies styles from a default arrow, pastes them onto a "large" arrow with the same arrowheads, and expects arrowheadSize to be undefined.

instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. minor (line 2074): actionChangeArrowheadSize uses `isLinearElement` only. The sibling actionChangeArrowhead also requires `canHaveArrowheads(element.type)`. As a result, choosing a size writes arrowheadSize onto selected line elements, which draw no heads. Also, with a line and a sized arrow selected together, getFormValue shows no selection in the control even though the only arrow has one size. The plan's rules 4 and 8 say isLinearElement, so this follows the plan but breaks the sibling convention. — fix: In perform, in the getFormValue value getter and in the isRelevant predicate, use `isLinearElement(el) && canHaveArrowheads(el.type)` (already imported) so that only arrows are read and written.

instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/arrowheadSize.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. minor (line 26): `as any` is used outside restore call sites (`element as any` in getSize, and `elements: any[]` in exportOne). Plan rule 4 allows `as any` only at restore call sites. Coverage gaps: no redo after undo, no check that choosing the size an arrow already has leaves the element unchanged (no version bump, no new key), and none of the other creation paths (flowchart, convertToShape, App.drawshape, ConvertElementTypePopup) is tested. — fix: Type getSize as `(element: ExcalidrawElement)` and exportOne as `(elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[])` (or the type restoreElements returns). Add a redo assertion to the undo test, and add a no-op test that clicks arrowheadSize-medium on a default arrow and expects the element's version to be unchanged.
